lines.text: Monday, 7:52 a.m. There's a number floating over every head at your school. And it tells you exactly how much that person secretly hates you.
The kid who says hi to you every single morning: 91 percent.
The quiet kid you've never talked to: 0.
Bro, why are you staring at everyone's foreheads?
Theo. Your best friend since kindergarten. 87 percent.
Are we... good?
What? Yeah. Obviously. Why?
In the next 7 days, you'll make more money than your parents make in a month, find out what Theo has been hiding for 6 years, and finally read the one number you've been too scared to look at.
The rules are simple. 0 means they like you. 100 means they'd push you into a pool in December. And it updates live.
You can't see your own. Mirrors, cameras and FaceTime don't work. You tried all 3.
Breakfast. Your mom: 12 percent.
Did you eat my yogurt again?
A 2016 study from MIT and Tel Aviv University asked students about their friendships. 95 percent thought their friends felt the same way about them. Only about half actually did.
So you spend the day reading the room. Literally.
Your math teacher, who gave you a C minus: 2 percent. She doesn't hate you. She hates grading.
The guy who copies your homework every day: 74.
A 2006 review of 206 studies found that people catch a lie only about 54 percent of the time. Basically a coin flip. You're now at 100.
But there's one number you won't look at. Maya. Third row, by the window. Every time she walks past, you suddenly find your shoes very interesting.
That night, YouTube recommends you a video. I made 10,000 dollars reselling sneakers at 16.
The whole trick is buying low. And the guy says the hard part is knowing how far you can push a seller before they walk away.
You look at the screen. Then at the ceiling. Then you text Theo.
How much do you know about sneakers?
Bro. Everything.
Saturday. A sneaker meetup in a parking garage. Theo spots the real ones. You read the sellers.
Jordan 4s. Never worn. 400.
70. Annoyed, but still listening.
95. Too far. One more dollar and he walks.
160. Cash. Right now.
98. Deal.
Kid, you're a nightmare.
That night, you list them for 650.
In 2022, the investment bank Cowen said the sneaker resale market could hit 30 billion dollars by 2030. You want your piece.
Every meetup, every app, every garage sale. You find every seller's limit, to the dollar.
By Friday, you and Theo have made 8,400 dollars. You pay for groceries, and your mom's number drops to 4.
But Theo's doesn't move. Counting cash with you. Laughing. 87.
Then, in your room, he sees it. On your shelf. The trophy from 4th grade.
You still have that?
First place, science fair. A volcano that shot foam 10 feet in the air. You remember presenting it. You never think about whose idea it was.
It was yours. Wasn't it.
I was sick that day. You said you'd tell them. You never did.
Monday. The city's teen business contest. First prize: 50,000 dollars. You enter the sneaker business. Theo almost doesn't come.
3 judges. All 3 start at 60. They've seen 40 pitches today.
So you pitch while reading them live. A joke: 55. The profit chart: 41. The part where you buy every pair 40 percent under market: 12.
Impressive. Last question. Whose idea was this?
Judges love a solo founder. You can see it. Every time you said I, their numbers dropped. And Theo is in the back row. 93.
Honestly? His. Theo picks every pair. I just do the talking. Like I did in 4th grade.
Theo's number starts falling. 70. 40. 9.
And the judges call you both up. First place. A giant cardboard check for 50,000 dollars, with 2 names on it.
The 9 is for when you spoiled the finale of my show.
Outside, someone is waiting by the doors. Maya. She saw the whole thing.
That was really cool. What you did for him.
And for the first time all week, you look up.
0. Not low. Zero. You've read 1,400 numbers this week. That's the 3rd zero you've ever seen. Your mom isn't one of them.
So... are you going to ask me out, or do I have to?
Yes. I mean, I am. The first one.
So. If you could see who secretly hates you, would you look? And whose number would you check first? Tell me in the comments.
